Closing to STOP an auto-merge that was never requested — reopening is the intended next step, and no work is lost.

This PR was opened as a **DRAFT** by `pr-opener` (the session MCP is 403 on PR writes). Seconds later `claude-pr-automerge` ran, marked it **ready for review**, and **enabled auto-merge (squash)** — its `open-and-automerge` job completed in 5s, which is the enable-and-return path, not the 8-minute poll fallback. `pytest-run` was in progress and would have merged this on green.

The session that opened it was instructed to open a draft and **not merge**. It cannot undo either action itself: `update_pull_request(draft:true)` returns 403 for the same reason `create_pull_request` did. Closing is the only lever it has, and it is fully reversible.

**Nothing is lost.** Branch `claude/automation-landing-orphans` is intact at `5b80ffd4` with the full body above. Reopen it (as a draft) to continue review.

⚠️ **This is itself a finding, and it is filed rather than just worked around.** `claude-pr-automerge.yml` declares `paths: ['.github/pr-automerge-requests/*.txt', '.github/pr-automerge-request']`, and this branch touched **neither** — its diff is `automation/**` and `docs/**` only. So a workflow whose single job unconditionally marks ready and enables auto-merge fired on a push that did not request it. Its own header already records this exact class once before: a `**` glob that *"armed auto-merge on THIS VERY PR by matching the directory's own README.md"*, with the lesson *"a trigger path that a doc edit can fire is a trigger that merges PRs nobody asked to merge."* That is the second instance, and the job body has no draft check and no request-file check to fall back on — the path filter is the only gate.

— MI-62, session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ
